product.amstrad-pc1386.summary: The lower-cost alternative to the PC2386, sold without a factory hard disk.
product.amstrad-pc1386.history: Amstrad announced the PC1386 in September 1989 as a lower-cost version of the PC2386 for the business market. In the United Kingdom the base unit started at £1,250, with a monitor sold separately.
product.amstrad-pc1386.technical.storage: Buyers could add a hard disk. Amstrad support says the unit shipped without one and that the installed disk type depended on the reseller.
product.amstrad-pc1386.technical.setup: The separate SETUP utility let users restore settings after the battery ran flat. Amstrad support lists this model.
product.amstrad-pc1386.technical.verifie: The model identity and commercial offer are documented. The BluMach entry is in research.
product.amstrad-pc1386.technical.limitat: A BIOS dump attributable to this model is needed to validate boot and video in BluMach.
product.amstrad-pc1386.technical.cpu: The exact 386 variant remains open. Retro Maniek lists a 386SX. Bob Morris told Cliff Lawson that he installed a Cyrix Cx486DRx2, which points to a 386DX.
